title: Cosmic Oddities
blurb: Moons, missions and planets that make less sense than your fake answers.

prompts.text: The Apollo 11 command module pilot, who orbited the Moon while his two crewmates landed, was Michael _____.
The tallest volcano in the solar system, Olympus Mons, is on the planet _____.
Sunsets on Mars look _____ instead of red.
Saturn is so light for its size that it would _____ in a big enough bathtub.
Pluto takes about _____ Earth years to orbit the Sun once.
The Sun holds about 99.8 percent of all the _____ in the solar system.
Before stepping onto the Moon, Buzz Aldrin quietly took _____ inside the lunar module.
A total solar eclipse is possible because the Sun is about _____ times wider than the Moon and also that many times farther away.
One year on Neptune lasts about _____ Earth years.
William Herschel discovered Uranus in 1781 and wanted to name it after King _____.
Voyager 1 carries a golden _____ filled with sounds and images of Earth.
In 1962 John Glenn became the first American to eat in space, squeezing _____ from a tube.
In weightlessness an astronaut's spine stretches out, which can make them up to _____ percent taller.
A day on Mars is called a _____.
Venus spins backwards compared with most planets, so the Sun rises in the _____ there.
The most volcanically active world in the solar system is Jupiter's moon _____.
Saturn's moon Titan has lakes of liquid methane and _____.
A comet's ion tail always points directly away from the _____.
The largest object in the asteroid belt is the dwarf planet _____.
Pluto was officially reclassified as a dwarf planet in _____.
The first woman in space, in 1963, was the Soviet cosmonaut Valentina _____.
Betelgeuse, a red supergiant, shines in the constellation _____.
The brightest star in Earth's night sky is _____.
NASA's Space Shuttle fleet was retired in _____.
The Apollo 13 mission was crippled when one of its _____ tanks exploded on the way to the Moon.
The Sun's outer atmosphere, the _____, is hundreds of times hotter than its visible surface.
The first pulsar was discovered in 1967 by the astronomer Jocelyn _____.
The last person to walk on the Moon, in December 1972, was Apollo 17's Eugene _____.
In 1998 the ashes of geologist Eugene Shoemaker were launched to the Moon aboard NASA's _____.
NASA's Mars Climate Orbiter was lost in 1999 after one team used imperial units and another used _____ units.
Saturn's north pole is capped by a giant storm with a very unusual shape: a _____.
Astronauts on the International Space Station see about _____ sunrises every day.
The densest planet in the solar system is _____.
Apollo astronauts said fresh moon dust smelled like spent _____.
NASA's Opportunity rover fell silent on Mars in 2018 after a planet-wide _____ storm blocked its sunlight.
NASA ended the Cassini mission in 2017 by plunging the probe into _____.
The James Webb Space Telescope launched on _____ Day in 2021.
We only ever see one side of the Moon because it is tidally _____ to Earth.
Mars has two small moons, Phobos and _____.
Venus is hotter than Mercury, even though Mercury is closer to the Sun, because its thick atmosphere causes a powerful _____ effect.
Mercury and _____ are the only two planets in the solar system with no moons.
The only spacecraft ever to visit Uranus and Neptune is _____.
The Apollo 11 lunar module that landed on the Moon in 1969 was named _____.
Pluto's largest moon is _____, so big that the two orbit a point in space between them.
The so-called dark side of the Moon gets just as much _____ as the side we see.
Exactly _____ people have ever walked on the Moon.
